Use More Engaging Prompts:: Ask the child more open-ended questions that require critical thinking and imagination.
Example: "Why do you think the big dogs are going out?"
Provide More Constructive Feedback:: Give more detailed responses to the child's answers to help them understand better.
Example: "That's right, it's a red fire truck! Fire trucks are often red so they can be easily seen when they're rushing to an emergency."
Expand More on the Child's Responses:: Provide additional information or context to help the child learn new vocabulary and concepts.
Example: "Yes, he said he doesn't like the hat. Maybe it looks too funny for him. What do you think makes a hat look nice?"
Repetition to Reinforce Learning:: Repeat prompts after expanding on the child's responses to reinforce learning.
Example: "He doesn’t like her hat. Can you say 'I do not like that hat' like he did?"
